newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares flat on results, U.S. rate news.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares flat on results, U.S. rate news.

text.p: Singapore shares ended the morning session flat on Wednesday as investors remained sidelined during the corporate reporting season and digested the likely impact of an overnight rise in U.S. interest rates.

"The question investors are asking is whether this is the start of a trend in rate hikes or a one-off," a dealer with a local firm said. "There's nothing else happening in Singapore to get their interest up," he added.
At the 0430 GMT lunchtime break, the key Straits Times Industrials Index was down 1.74 at 2,098.21.
Morning trade was slow with traded volume a thin 72.4 million units producing 198 gainers and 92 losers.
Frozen seafood company Pacific Andes was the morning's most active counter, up US$0.025 to US$0.745.
Vickers Ballas maintained early momentum to end the morning session up Singapore $0.24 at S$2.48 on news of a bonus share issue and 1996 net profits up 41 percent.
Top gainer in the morning was North Borneo Timber, up a solid S$0.30 to S$11.00. Losers were led by Creative Technology, down S$0.30 to S$14.50.
